meta.title: The Shy Octopus
meta.textType: story: a trip to the aquarium

paragraphs: On Saturday, November fourteenth, the Explorers went to the town aquarium with Teacher Kim. They arrived at half past nine, and they watched the feeding show at ten o'clock. Mia carried her digital camera around her neck. "I want a photo of the octopus," she said. "Then let's go to its tank," said Lily. At half past ten, they stood in front of a big tank with rocks and a clay pot.

A keeper stood next to the tank. "The octopus is shy," she said. "If you wait quietly, it will come out." "Where is it?" asked May. "It is in the clay pot," said the keeper. "An octopus can change color to hide itself, so look carefully." Mia stepped to the glass and held up her camera. The other children stood behind her.

Five minutes passed, and nothing moved. "Is it still in the pot?" asked Lily. Leo turned to May and whispered, "Perhaps he has gone shopping." May laughed quietly, but she did not look away. "I can't wait anymore," said Leo, "but Mia is as still as a rock." It was a quarter to eleven. "Mia has waited here since half past ten," said Lily. "She has not moved for fifteen minutes." Even the keeper smiled.

Suddenly, at ten to eleven, a long orange arm came out of the clay pot. "Look!" whispered Mia. She did not move her feet, and she took the photo. Then the whole octopus appeared at the glass. It held the glass with its arms, and its color changed from orange to red. "I am so excited!" said Leo. "It is a beautiful creature," said the keeper, "but it is very shy."

Mia looked at the photo on her camera and smiled. The orange arm and the clay pot were clear. "Mia waited, so we all saw a real octopus," said Teacher Kim. "Can I put the photo on the blog?" asked Mia. "Yes, but I will read the post first," said Teacher Kim. Leo looked at the empty pot and smiled. "Now the octopus can go shopping," he said.
text.summary: The Explorers visit the town aquarium. Mia waits at the glass for the shy octopus, and her friends wait with her. At last an orange arm comes out of the pot, and Mia takes the photo.

sentences.text: On Saturday, November fourteenth, the Explorers went to the town aquarium with Teacher Kim.
They arrived at half past nine, and they watched the feeding show at ten o'clock.
Mia carried her digital camera around her neck.
"I want a photo of the octopus," she said.
"Then let's go to its tank," said Lily.
At half past ten, they stood in front of a big tank with rocks and a clay pot.
A keeper stood next to the tank.
"The octopus is shy," she said.
"If you wait quietly, it will come out."
"Where is it?" asked May.
"It is in the clay pot," said the keeper.
"An octopus can change color to hide itself, so look carefully."
Mia stepped to the glass and held up her camera.
The other children stood behind her.
Five minutes passed, and nothing moved.
"Is it still in the pot?" asked Lily.
Leo turned to May and whispered, "Perhaps he has gone shopping."
May laughed quietly, but she did not look away.
"I can't wait anymore," said Leo, "but Mia is as still as a rock."
It was a quarter to eleven.
"Mia has waited here since half past ten," said Lily.
"She has not moved for fifteen minutes."
Even the keeper smiled.
Suddenly, at ten to eleven, a long orange arm came out of the clay pot.
"Look!" whispered Mia.
She did not move her feet, and she took the photo.
Then the whole octopus appeared at the glass.
It held the glass with its arms, and its color changed from orange to red.
"I am so excited!" said Leo.
"It is a beautiful creature," said the keeper, "but it is very shy."
Mia looked at the photo on her camera and smiled.
The orange arm and the clay pot were clear.
"Mia waited, so we all saw a real octopus," said Teacher Kim.
"Can I put the photo on the blog?" asked Mia.
"Yes, but I will read the post first," said Teacher Kim.
Leo looked at the empty pot and smiled.
"Now the octopus can go shopping," he said.
